prompt.en: Two nearby radios still use identical repeater memories for a direct test. Each transmits below its receive frequency. The repeater is off, and neither hears the other. Which setting change addresses this mismatch?

text.en: Keep the split frequencies and change only the access tone.

feedback.en: An access tone can open a tone-controlled squelch, but it cannot move speech between different frequencies.

text.en: Set both radios to transmit and receive on the same suitable simplex channel.

feedback.en: A shared simplex channel aligns each transmitter with the other receiver. Check reliable copy in both directions.

text.en: Reverse both offsets but keep their receive frequencies unchanged.

feedback.en: Both radios would still listen away from where the other transmits. Reversing identical offsets preserves a mismatch.

text.en: Swap transmit and receive in both memories, keeping a split between them.

feedback.en: Both radios would again share a transmit frequency different from their shared receive frequency. Swapping both split memories leaves a mismatch.

explanation.en: A repeater moves speech between its input and output frequencies. Without it, both radios need a suitable shared simplex channel and reliable copy in both directions.

prompt.en: An illustrative repeater output is 146.880 MHz with a negative 600 kHz offset. Which transmit frequency belongs in the radio memory?

feedback.en: Adding 0.600 MHz gives a positive offset. The stated offset is negative, so subtract.
This is the output you listen to. Transmitting there would ignore the split.
600 kHz = 0.600 MHz. Subtracting gives 146.280 MHz, below the output.
This subtracts 0.060 MHz, or 60 kHz. Convert 600 kHz to 0.600 MHz first.

explanation.en: Convert 600 kHz to 0.600 MHz before subtracting. A negative offset puts transmit below the repeater output.

prompt.en: A transmitter passes a long dummy-load test without reported interference. For a later antenna test at the same dial setting, which next step uses that result appropriately?

text.en: Check the channel and make a brief on-air test; the earlier load test did not test sharing the airwaves.

feedback.en: The dummy load absorbed RF locally. An antenna sends it into a shared channel, so listen and keep the radiated test brief.

text.en: Repeat the full-length test on the antenna; the unchanged dial setting makes the earlier result applicable.

feedback.en: The dial setting stayed fixed, but the RF path changed from a load to an antenna. Other users can now receive the test.

text.en: Lower microphone gain and repeat the long test; reduced audio makes another channel check unnecessary.

feedback.en: Audio drive affects modulation, not whether RF reaches other users. A quiet carrier can still interfere.

text.en: Match the antenna with the tuner and repeat the long test; the new match gives the same RF containment as the load.

feedback.en: A tuner changes the impedance seen by the radio. It does not absorb the signal instead of radiating it.

explanation.en: A dummy load absorbs RF locally. An antenna radiates into shared spectrum, so the on-air test still needs a channel check and a brief transmission.
